newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwaitis to protest against Israel in parliament.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaitis to protest against Israel in parliament.

text.p: A group of Kuwaitis plan to hold an anti-Israel gathering on Tuesday inside parliament after being denied the right to hold a demonstration outside the house, security sources said.
Security sources told Reuters that the governorate of Kuwait City turned down a request by the group to gather outside parliament on Tuesday to protest against Israeli policies.
"They now plan to gather inside parliament and want to hold a news conference to express their views," one source said.
Security sources said the group included Sunni Moslem and Shi'ite members, Islamists and liberals.

Kuwait does not have direct relations with Israel and refuses to nomalise ties with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for appearing to side with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of the Gulf Arab state.

As in most Arab and Moslem countries, the start of work last month on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem has triggered strong condemnation in Kuwait which has agreed with other Arab states to stop the normalisation of ties with Israel.

"What is required is to severe ties with the Zionist entity and to abandon the option of negotiations that has proved its failure to all," said al-Mujtama' weekly, the mouthpiece of the Social Reform Society which is widely believed to be Kuwait's version of the Moslem Brotherhood.
"The way of Jihad (holy war) is the only way to restore rights. Jews do not respect pledges."
